_note: Combat FX numbers (docs/pivot/combat_api.md 4.6, 4.7, 4.8; Technical Artist). Read by scripts/combat/fx/combat_fx.gd, and by OrbitCamera for `shake.<id>` (amplitude_m, duration_s, frequency_hz). Distances in metres, times in seconds of REAL time unless it says 'combat clock'. Colours are hex. Anything above the glow threshold blooms in the PS2 look, so 'intensity' and 'glow' values above 1 are the bright ones. Names and numbers are Level 1: change freely.

sparks._note: streak bursts. count, speed [min, max] m/s, life_s, length_m and width_m of each streak, gravity m/s2, cone_deg around the hit normal, flash = the bright pop (size_m, life_s, intensity), ring = optional expanding ring.

shake_scale_note: Robot scale test (CS-21, Technical Artist). Footfall and landing shakes per scale. amplitude_m is tuned for a camera for_camera_m metres away; pass suggested_mult to the camera so a far camera still shakes (a 75 m camera needs a bigger offset for the same angle). The camera caps amplitude * mult at CameraShake.MAX_AMPLITUDE_M (0.25 m): raise that cap for the huge robot or the shake will not read.

dust._note: Footstep dust and landing slams per scale (robot scale test CS-21; scripts/combat/fx/scale_dust.gd reads these). Bigger and slower at large scale: count puffs fly out from a ring of ring_radius_m at speed_mps (min, max), each puff is size_m (min, max) wide at the start and grows by `grow` times by the end of life_s, rises at rise_mps, and fades from `alpha`. gravity is m/s2 (negative pulls down slowly). shock_ring (slams only) is a flat ring on the floor that expands to max_m. Distances in metres, times in seconds of real time.

scale_sets._note: Which shake and dust each robot scale uses (the Gameplay Programmer reads this). footfalls_s are the seconds in the baked walk and run clips at playback speed 1.0 where each foot comes down (lowest foot bone: left first, then right); divide by the playback speed you play the clip at. The same clips drive both robots, so the times are shared.

hit_flash._note: Tuning v1.3 (Ross: chunky hits): the struck model turns flat opaque white for duration_s of REAL time as a hit lands (so you see it inside the hit-stop freeze), then snaps back. Read by scripts/combat/fx/hit_flash.gd through combat_fx.gd. `outcomes` is per hit outcome: on/off, `brightness` (1.0 = pure white, lower = a greyer flash) and `duration_mult`. `require_damage`: a hit that took nothing off (a sealed core, a sword clinking off a relay) does not flash. `player.enabled` is Red's own flash when she is hit (off; the F12 knob 'Flash Red when she is hit' turns it on). The F12 knob 'White impact flash' switches the whole thing off.

hit_sound._note: Tuning v1.3: every landed hit plays its sound (the move's own sfx, else by weight: light, air, heavy, launch). pitch_var is the random spread of pitch around 1.0 for a landed hit (so it never sounds the same twice in a row); heavy_pitch_var is the same for the heavy and launch sounds (tighter, so the big ones stay deep). It goes through AudioManager.play_sfx(id, pitch_mult).

telegraph._note: the wind-up flash and the converging ring that lands exactly on impact: a parry cue. kinds are picked by info.telegraph_kind, else 'parryable' / 'unparryable' from the signal; add kinds freely (dodge_only, unblockable ...) and the cue appears with no code change.

flare._note: the Lamp Flare: a lamp burst on Red, a shock ring, and a cooler, calmer world while enemies run slow. Envelope: burst_s ramps to the peak, then holds, then fades over fade_s at the end.

lights_on._note: Lights On: Red's edge light and the neon strips on her jacket brighten, her lamp stays lit, a burst on activation.

dash._note: speed streaks left behind a dash. heights are metres above her feet.

sounds._note: who plays what (combat_api.md 4.6). A move's own sfx / swing.sfx wins over these. The HUD plays combat_noise_rank_up and combat_lock_on, so they are NOT here.
